notes.title: v1.0.9 - Oculus/WMR Comfort Tweaks, Sensei Movement Overrides!
notes.content:
v1.0.9 - 2018-12-18

This update is all about gameplay comfort.  We made a number of adjustments to make Oculus Rift and WMR feel right.  The majority of this game was developed on one HTC Vive, so forgive us for getting to this a bit late.

We also are including a highly requested feature, which is the ability to make the Sensei stay in place regardless of the song and beatmap.  We'll discuss more about how that works below.

Features:
* HMD Comfort Tweaks
- Oculus Rift
-- Throw ninja star action moved from thumbstick click to A/X button
-- Hands default to more comfortable rotation on first time launch.  This does not override your hand rotation settings if you already have one saved.
- Windows MR 
-- Haptics have been tweaked slightly.  They are a bit subtle, but they are working.  If you're still getting absolutely no haptics, see this link (https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/mixed-reality/updating-your-steamvr-application-for-windows-mixed-reality#haptics)
- HMD-specific tooltips on main menu screen

* Sensei Movement Override is live!  
- After selecting a beatmap, you'll see a new On/Off toggle above the song description.  The toggle defaults to the value stored in the beatmap file, but can be changed by hitting On or Off with a ninja star.  This means you can make 360 degree beatmaps stationary and vice-versa.  Changing the setting with this toggle will not overwrite the value stored in the file.
- Each beatmap will now have 2 possible leaderboards.  One for each option of the Sensei Movement Override.  So if it is set to On, you'll be placed on the leaderboard with others who have played with the setting On, and same for Off.

* Each leaderboard now shows a maximum of 20 scores, previously was 10 scores.

Bug Fixes:
* Fixed the beatmap selection to where you don't have to "double click" beatmaps to activate them and unhide the Start button.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33276564/8994307bf4d7b809f61313480cc4318557f4107c.gif[/img]

notes.title: v1.0.8 - Sound FX Update - Boom. Bap. Pow.
notes.content:
v1.0.8 - 2018-12-04

Features:
* We now have sound effects for the following actions:
 - In Menu
    -- Ninja Star throw
    -- Ninja Star impact
 - In Game
    -- Board hit
    -- Cinderblock hit
    -- Item missed "whoosh"
* We now have volume settings (0-10) for each of the above categories.  If you're used to playing without the hit/miss sound effects, this gives you an easy way to turn them off.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33276564/88fc61aa48498ad4fe7b9d7e844204354dd02a48.png[/img]

We know that this was a big one for a lot of you, and we hope that this first pass makes the game more enjoyable for you.  We'll continue tweaking the sounds, and would appreciate your feedback about which sounds you're liking and which aren't quite where they need to be yet.  

As always, join us in Discord to let us know what you think! 
https://discord.gg/Yq3dzm2

notes.title: v1.0.7 - No Room Left Behind
notes.content:
v1.0.7 - 2018-11-27

It's been a month!  Sorry!  I was in Asia!

Features
* In Settings, you can now adjust the depth, or distance from center, of the targets where items will land during gameplay.  This is in addition to the existing setting that lets you adjust height.  The goal here is to support rooms and reaches of all sizes, and to give you the exact gameplay experience you want.  Want the items to land right up in your dern grill?  Go for it.  Want to have to lunge forward to hit items?  Live your best life.

See it in action here:
https://gfycat.com/ShowyUnimportantGreatwhiteshark

Let us know on Discord if you encounter any issues!

notes.title: v1.0.3 - All Your Memory Are Belong to You
notes.content:
v1.0.3 - 2018-10-01

That's right, we skipped a whole patch version!

Optimizations
We fixed two pretty gnarly memory issues.  Both were a result of importing tracks, but let's discuss each individually.

1. Audio data for all tracks imported from StreamingAssets was staying in memory indefinitely.  Even when compressed, this caused a considerable amount of bloat.  For 16 imported tracks we saw almost 2GB worth of unnecessary memory usage by Audio Clips.  To fix this, we modified the import behavior to store file pointers to imported audio files instead of loading audio data on start.  While this was a win, when we built the executable and loaded it up we still saw considerable bloat when importing a lot of tracks.  That takes us to issue #2! 
2. Those weren't really file pointers at all!  The WWW File objects themselves are quite bloaty as well.  So, while our memory usage by Audio Clips looked great, we were still seeing up to 1GB of bloat when importing the same 16 tracks.  For this, we deferred all File and Audio access until it was needed - when previewing, mapping, or playing a track.  We then unload and dealloc all File and Audio objects when they are no longer being used.

The result of the 2 fixes is that "no matter how many" (probably) tracks you import, you should never see memory bloat larger than that of the most-recently-used audio track.  For a lengthy WAV file this was less than 100MB when we tested.

That's it.  Less scary bug fixes and tweaks are coming soon!
